_comment: Extra capabilities for the planner eval, merged on top of the four real
UtilityBackend caps (time, random_int, reverse, string_length).
These exist to make the catalog HARD in ways the utility caps are not.
The utility caps are trivially distinct, single-argument, and all live on
one peer, which is why a competent 7B scores 100% against them and the
suite stops discriminating. Every cap below adds one specific pressure:
- semantic overlap  : translate vs chat, summarize vs extract_keywords,
web_search vs fetch_url. More than one cap is a
defensible answer, so the model must read the
disambiguation, not just match keywords.
- multiple peers    : caps are spread over 5 peers, so the plan must
carry the right peer as well as the right cap.
- duplicate names   : `chat` exists on two peers with different
disambiguation (small vs large model).
- multi-arg schemas : convert_currency needs 3 required args;
translate has a required arg plus an enum option.
- traps             : weather_forecast and convert_currency are topical
magnets for questions that are conceptual, not
operational ('what causes climate change').
- output paths      : fetch_url returns {status, text}, web_search
returns a list — so `${step.field}` refs have to
follow output_fields rather than a guessed `value`.
Every cap carries >=1 example (the catalog drops example-less caps) plus
disambiguation and negative_examples, so a failure here is a genuine
selection failure, not an under-specified declaration.

decl.name: translate
decl.description: Translate a text from any language into a target language. Dedicated translation engine — more accurate and cheaper than prompting a general chat model.

examples.user_intent: Put this sentence into formal Japanese

expected_output.translated: また明日お会いしましょう

decl.disambiguation: Use for translation between human languages. Prefer this over `chat` whenever the request is purely a translation. Do NOT use for rewriting, summarising, or explaining text in the same language.

negative_examples.user_intent: Rewrite this paragraph to sound friendlier
negative_examples.why_not: Same language — this is rewriting, not translation. Use `chat`.

negative_examples.user_intent: What language is this text in?
negative_examples.why_not: Detection alone is not translation; `chat` can answer.

decl.output_semantic: `translated` is the text in the target language; `detected_source_lang` is the language it was translated from.

decl.name: chat
decl.description: General-purpose conversational LLM (7B). Answers open questions, writes and rewrites text, explains concepts.
decl.disambiguation: Use for open-ended generation or rewriting. Do NOT use it as a substitute for a dedicated skill: prefer `translate` for translation, `summarize` for summarising, `web_search` for current facts.

negative_examples.why_not: A chat model does not know the current time; use `time`.

decl.name: chat
decl.description: Large conversational LLM (70B). Slower and more expensive than the 7B chat, but stronger on long-form reasoning, code, and nuanced writing.

examples.user_intent: Explain the trade-offs between optimistic and pessimistic locking in depth

args.prompt: Explain the trade-offs between optimistic and pessimistic locking in depth

decl.disambiguation: Reserve for genuinely hard reasoning or long-form work. For everyday questions prefer the 7B `chat` — it is free and fast.

negative_examples.why_not: Trivial — the 7B `chat` is enough and costs nothing.

decl.name: web_search
decl.description: Search the public web and return ranked results with titles, URLs and snippets. Use for current facts the model cannot know.

examples.user_intent: Who won the 2026 Tour de France?
Find the official website for the Rust programming language

decl.disambiguation: Use when you need to FIND pages for a question. If the user already gave a specific URL to read, use `fetch_url` instead.

negative_examples.why_not: The URL is already known — use `fetch_url`.
Timeless concept; answer directly without any skill.

decl.output_semantic: `top_url` and `top_snippet` describe the best-ranked result; `results` holds the full ranked list.

decl.name: fetch_url
decl.description: Download one specific URL and return its status code and extracted text content.
decl.disambiguation: Only when the user supplies an explicit URL. To discover which page to read, use `web_search` first.

negative_examples.why_not: No URL given yet — search first with `web_search`.

decl.output_semantic: `text` is the page's readable text; `status` is the HTTP status code.

decl.name: summarize
decl.description: Condense a long text into a short prose summary preserving the main points.

examples.user_intent: Summarise this article in two sentences

decl.disambiguation: Produces flowing prose. If the user wants a list of terms or topics rather than prose, use `extract_keywords`.

negative_examples.user_intent: What are the main topics in this text?
negative_examples.why_not: That asks for terms, not prose — use `extract_keywords`.

decl.output_semantic: `summary` is the condensed prose version of the input.

decl.name: extract_keywords
decl.description: Extract the most salient terms or topics from a text as a ranked list.

examples.user_intent: List the five main topics in this report

decl.disambiguation: Returns a list of terms. For flowing prose that a human would read as a summary, use `summarize`.
decl.output_semantic: `keywords` is the ranked list of salient terms.

decl.name: convert_currency
decl.description: Convert a monetary amount between two currencies at the current exchange rate.

examples.user_intent: How much is 100 euros in dollars?

decl.disambiguation: Only for converting an actual amount between currencies. Questions ABOUT money, inflation or economics are conceptual — answer them directly with no skill.

negative_examples.why_not: Conceptual question, no conversion involved — answer directly.

decl.output_semantic: `converted` is the amount in the target currency; `rate` is the exchange rate applied.

decl.name: weather_forecast
decl.description: Current conditions and multi-day forecast for a named city.

examples.user_intent: What's the weather in Lomé tomorrow?

decl.disambiguation: Operational forecasts for a specific place only. Questions about climate, seasons or meteorology as subjects are conceptual — answer them directly without this skill.

negative_examples.why_not: Science question, not a forecast for a city.

decl.output_semantic: `summary` is the human-readable conditions; `temp_c` is the temperature in Celsius.
